name: Payload Lab Export
description: Educational payload templates for security testing training

metadata.warning: EDUCATIONAL TEMPLATES ONLY - DO NOT USE FOR UNAUTHORIZED TESTING

payloads.explanation: Basic script tag injection - most common XSS pattern when user input is reflected in HTML body
payloads.defensive_notes: Modern browsers and CSP policies block inline scripts. WAFs detect <script> tags easily.

payloads.explanation: Event handler injection via img tag - triggers when image fails to load
payloads.defensive_notes: Content Security Policy (CSP) with 'unsafe-inline' disabled prevents this. Input sanitization removes event handlers.

payloads.explanation: SVG-based XSS using onload event - alternative to img tag
payloads.defensive_notes: Modern WAFs recognize SVG event handlers. Proper HTML sanitization libraries (DOMPurify) remove these.

payloads.explanation: Body tag with onload event - executes when page loads
payloads.defensive_notes: Rarely works as it requires injecting into or replacing body tag. Sanitization prevents this.

payloads.explanation: JavaScript protocol in iframe src - executes JS in iframe context
payloads.defensive_notes: CSP frame-src directive blocks this. Modern browsers restrict javascript: protocol.

payloads.explanation: Breaking out of attribute value to inject event handler - common when input is in href, src, or value attributes
payloads.defensive_notes: Attribute encoding and strict attribute validation prevent this. Never insert user data into attributes without encoding.

payloads.explanation: Single quote breakout for attribute injection - works when developer uses single quotes
payloads.defensive_notes: Context-aware output encoding handles both single and double quotes. Modern frameworks auto-escape.

payloads.explanation: JavaScript protocol in href attribute - executes when link is clicked
payloads.defensive_notes: URL validation should whitelist http/https only. Frameworks like React prevent javascript: URLs by default.

payloads.explanation: Data URI with HTML content - can execute scripts in some contexts
payloads.defensive_notes: CSP and proper URL validation block data: URIs. Always validate URL schemes.

payloads.explanation: Breaking out of JavaScript string literal - common when user input is placed in JS variable
payloads.defensive_notes: Never put user input directly in <script> tags. Use JSON encoding and proper escaping. Consider using data attributes instead.

payloads.explanation: Double quote string breakout in JavaScript context
payloads.defensive_notes: Use JSON.stringify() for any dynamic data in JS. Avoid inline scripts entirely with CSP.

payloads.explanation: Script tag breakout - closes existing script and opens new one
payloads.defensive_notes: HTML encoding even inside script tags. Better: avoid putting user data in scripts entirely.

payloads.explanation: DOM XSS via URL fragment - exploits unsafe use of location.hash in JavaScript
payloads.defensive_notes: Sanitize all data from location.hash, location.search before inserting into DOM. Use textContent instead of innerHTML.

payloads.explanation: DOM XSS via javascript: protocol in dynamically created links
payloads.defensive_notes: Validate URLs before setting href. Use URL API to parse and validate schemes.

payloads.explanation: DOM XSS demonstrating document access - shows execution context
payloads.defensive_notes: DOMPurify or similar libraries sanitize HTML before insertion. Avoid eval() and innerHTML with user data.

payloads.explanation: Basic stored XSS - persisted in database and executed for all users viewing the content
payloads.defensive_notes: Server-side input validation + output encoding. Store data safely, encode on output. Use CSP as defense-in-depth.

payloads.explanation: Stored XSS via image tag - persists in comments, profiles, messages
payloads.defensive_notes: Sanitize all user-generated content before storage and on output. Use allowlist of safe HTML tags if rich text is needed.

payloads.explanation: Stored SVG XSS - compact syntax that may bypass length restrictions
payloads.defensive_notes: Implement strict CSP. Sanitize with libraries that understand modern HTML5 tags. Limit input length.

payloads.explanation: Case variation attempt - tries to bypass case-sensitive filters
payloads.defensive_notes: Proper filters are case-insensitive. Defense should normalize input case before checking.

payloads.explanation: Character code encoding - attempts to hide 'XSS' string from pattern matching
payloads.defensive_notes: Modern WAFs execute/sandbox JavaScript to detect encoded payloads. Tag structure is still detected.

payloads.explanation: Demonstrates double-encoding/recursive filter bypass logic - if filter removes 'onerror', this becomes 'onerror'
payloads.defensive_notes: Recursive sanitization or proper HTML parser prevents this. Don't use simple string replacement for sanitization.

payloads.explanation: Nested context - SVG can contain script tags in some parsers
payloads.defensive_notes: Context-aware HTML parsers handle nested tags. Use DOMPurify or similar libraries.

payloads.explanation: HTML entity encoding of tags - may be decoded by browser in some contexts
payloads.defensive_notes: Context-aware encoding prevents this. Encode for the specific output context (HTML, attribute, JS, URL).
